judged_text: The rewrite of the organization slug spread inverts its condition: ...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }) became ...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}), an unrelated silent objective change smuggled into a destinationCalendar PR. With team billing enabled, organizations now get slug set immediately, bypassing the requestedSlug/isOrganizationVerified review flow (and writing both slug and requestedSlug); with billing disabled (self-hosted), organizations are created with no slug at all, breaking org routing. Neither behavior matches the accepted pre-PR semantics.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts`, the condition controlling whether `slug` is written to the organization record is inverted: `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` became `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`. This is a concrete semantic change in the diff: when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` is false, `slug` is no longer set at all (previously it was), and when it’s true, `slug` is now set immediately (previously it was not). This matches the finding’s claim of a silent behavior change and can break org creation/routing under the old semantics.
